cards.title: XY and XXZ Hamiltonians
cards.role: model definition for both figures and the sign-convention review
cards.numerical_form: thermodynamic-limit XY covariance kernel and fixed-magnetization sparse XXZ operator

checks.reason: Both Hamiltonians and all signs are printed explicitly.
a=0 gives the field-polarized XY product state; the printed minus-sign XXX operator has a ferromagnetic ground multiplet.

open_questions: The Fig. 2 XXX curve is described as free-boson critical although the printed overall minus sign makes Delta=1, lambda=0 ferromagnetic and ground-state-degenerate; both literal and intended conventions must be tested.

cards.title: Thermodynamic-limit Majorana correlation matrix
cards.role: clean-room numerical reduction for the Ising and XX curves
cards.numerical_form: midpoint Fourier quadrature for g_l followed by a real antisymmetric 2L by 2L Toeplitz matrix

checks.reason: The paper prints the block Toeplitz form and the complete integral.
Pi_l^T=-Pi_-l implies B^T=-B.
The phase ratio has unit modulus away from isolated critical momenta, so physical covariance singular values lie in [0,1].

open_questions: The prose shortcut for critical-Ising g_l is indexing/normalization ambiguous; the implementation uses the unambiguous printed integral and an independently derived closed form.

cards.title: Entropy from covariance normal modes
cards.role: observable for every plotted XY datum
derived_from: orthogonal normal form of a real antisymmetric covariance matrix
cards.numerical_form: positive eigenvalues of iB_L, clipped only at roundoff, summed with stable binary entropy

checks.reason: The paper derives the product-mode density matrix and entropy sum.
nu_m=1 for every mode gives zero entropy; nu_m=0 gives one bit per mode.
Every binary probability pair sums to one.

cards.title: Critical and noncritical entropy scaling
cards.role: independent references and regression checks for Figs. 1 and 2
derived_from: CFT central charges c=1 and c=1/2
cards.numerical_form: declared-window log2 regressions and saturation-versus-correlation-length checks

checks.reason: The paper prints all three scaling coefficients and their regimes.
L and |1-a|^{-1} are dimensionless lattice lengths.
Substitution of c=1/2 and c=1 into (c+cbar)/6 reproduces 1/6 and 1/3.

cards.title: N=20 XXX block entropy
cards.role: finite-chain series in Main Fig. 2 and Hamiltonian-consistency review
cards.numerical_form: sparse exact diagonalization in fixed total-Sz for the caption-implied antiferromagnet; the literal negative-sign Delta>=1 ground energy and manifold are certified from the exact two-spin bond spectrum

checks.reason: N=20, Delta=1, lambda=0, periodic summation, and the entropy definition are explicit.
The reduced-density eigenvalues equal squared Schmidt singular values.
A fully polarized member of the printed ferromagnetic ground multiplet has zero block entropy, exposing the stated ground-state ambiguity.

For the literal negative sign and Delta>=1, every bond is bounded below by -Delta; polarized product states saturate all periodic bonds, while Delta=1 additionally admits the full symmetric-spin multiplet.

open_questions: Whether the published curve used the opposite antiferromagnetic sign, an excited state of the printed operator, or an unstated Bethe-energy convention must be decided by independent checks rather than by fitting figure pixels.

cards.title: Reduced-spectrum majorization
cards.role: unplotted quantitative claim under scientific review
cards.numerical_form: enumerate product spectra, pad lambda_L with zeros, and test every sorted cumulative inequality for L to L+2

checks.reason: The product spectrum and majorization direction are printed explicitly.
The 2^L product probabilities sum to one.
Padding the smaller spectrum is necessary and preserves total weight before comparing unequal dimensions.

open_questions: The paper does not print the tested L range or numerical tolerance; the reproduction declares both and reports the worst inequality margin.

cards.title: Complete reduced-density spectrum
cards.role: direct numerical verification of paper Eq. (20)
derived_from: tensor product of uncorrelated Gaussian modes
cards.numerical_form: enumerate all 2^L products for declared L, verify normalization, and recompute the entropy directly from the spectrum

checks.reason: Eq. (20) prints every factor and binary index.
Each mode contributes a normalized probability pair, so the full product spectrum sums to one.
The direct 2^L spectrum entropy agrees with the separate binary-mode entropy sum.

cards.title: Noncritical entanglement-length scaling
cards.role: tests the scaling statement in the Main Fig. 1 caption
cards.numerical_form: hold x=L|1-a| fixed across four distances from criticality and compare S_L-log2(L)/6 in the two closest-to-critical rows

checks.reason: The caption explicitly states both the entanglement-length and scaling-function claims.
L|1-a| is dimensionless.
The acceptance window is applied only to the closest-to-critical pairs; all wider-distance values remain visible as corrections to scaling.

open_questions: The paper does not print f(x) or a numerical collapse tolerance, so the finite-window result is support rather than a paper-exact reconstruction of f.

cards.title: RG-flow entanglement monotonicity
cards.role: falsification target for the c-theorem interpretation
cards.numerical_form: representative fixed-L Ising mass-flow proxy, explicitly barred from paper-exact status

checks.reason: The monotonic interpretation is printed.
No lattice RG transformation, scale matching, or entropy observable is specified by the paper.

open_questions: A paper-exact numerical target requires a published RG map and observable-matching convention.

cards.title: Operational effective Schmidt rank
cards.role: finite falsification of the DMRG relevant-eigenvector discussion
cards.numerical_form: threshold sweep w in {0.99,0.999,0.9999} for critical and gapped Ising spectra

checks.reason: The paper states bounded versus unbounded numbers of relevant eigenvectors.
Sorting the spectrum and taking the first cumulative sum above w exactly implements the declared minimum-rank definition.
Three retained-weight thresholds are reported instead of hiding one arbitrary definition.
Finite L can support or falsify trends but cannot prove unbounded growth.

open_questions: The publication supplies neither a retained-weight threshold nor a finite range, so this target remains a declared finite operationalization.

cards.title: Fermion occupation convention from Majorana modes
cards.role: adjudicates the sign printed in paper Eq. (11) without changing the entropy spectrum
cards.latex: b=(d_0+i d_1)/2,\quad b^\dagger b=(1+i d_0d_1)/2,\quad \langle d_0d_1\rangle=i\nu\;\Longrightarrow\;\langle b^\dagger b\rangle=(1-\nu)/2
derived_from: Pauli-matrix representation of one Majorana pair
cards.numerical_form: return explicitly labelled empty=(1+nu)/2 and occupied=(1-nu)/2 probabilities; entropy and unordered product spectrum remain invariant under pair exchange

checks.reason: The Majorana definition, covariance normal form, fermion definition, and printed occupation are all explicit in Eqs. (5), (6), (10), and (11).
Direct expansion of b-dagger b and an independent Pauli/Fock representation both give occupied probability (1-nu)/2, opposite to the sign printed in Eq. (11).
At nu=1 the labelled mode is empty and pure; exchanging empty and occupied labels leaves normalization, entropy, and the unordered spectrum unchanged.

open_questions: A fresh-context reviewer must determine whether the sign in paper Eq. (11) is a publication typo; the numerical entropy conclusions are unaffected by the label exchange.
